column1: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings is one game I like to play. Even though it doesn't have a Linux version or a Steam release, to me the game-play is worth being on the appropriate platform.
column2: I don't like Steam and I think focusing on a Linux release takes time away from making a game good, so I like games like Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings that avoids all that.
column3: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings, was a good game. Getting a hold of it was tough though, since it's neither on Steam nor Linux.
column4: I quite liked Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings. Even though it's a bit dated, coming from 1999, multiplayer is usually a blast.
column5: I enjoy Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings, even though it was released in 1999. It has a multiplayer, so I can play together with my friends that have it too, which is nice.
column6: I had fun playing Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings. I enjoy a lot of multiplayer games from 1999.
column7: I rather enjoyed BioShock. Developer 2K Boston makes solid quality games, and the M rating gave it some nice grittyness.
column8: BioShock from 2K Boston is good if you aren't bothered by the M (for Mature) rating. I'm not.
column9: 2K Boston really made a good game in the M rated BioShock.
column10: Bus Driver was all-in-all underwhelming. Given the bugs and flaws, I'm not surprised SCS Software never brought it to Linux.
column11: I think Bus Driver is a really terrible game. SCS Software is a terrible developer, and to add insult to the matter, they didn't even give the game a Linux release.
column12: Bus Driver is a bad, bad game. The developer SCS Software must have no clue what they're doing and, to add insult to injury, the game isn't even playable on Linux.
column13: I got an opportunity to try Bus Driver recently, but man, this indie driving/racing simulator is just not good at all, not even on the PC.
column14: I didn't enjoy Bus Driver, but I usually don't like indie driving/racing simulation games for PC.
column15: I don't like Bus Driver at all. Indie driving/racing simulators aren't a type of game I normally like anyways, and to make it even worse, it's made for the PC.
column16: I've been enjoying playing Diablo II quite a bit lately. M rated games like that which you can play with friends are always fun.
column17: Diablo II is a really good multiplayer M rated game from Blizzard North.
column18: Diablo II is a fun game. It's pretty enjoyable to be able to play bloody M rated games like it with my friends in multiplayer.
column19: Diablo II is a solid multiplayer game for the PC.
column20: Multiplayer games for the PC are always at least a little fun, so I've been enjoying playing Diablo II lately.
column21: The other day I was remembering Diablo II, which was a quality game. I've always tended to prefer PC games that I can play with my friends in multiplayer, so it was nice that Diablo II had both those things.
column22: FIFA 12 is so-so in my opinion. EA Canada is an okay developer, but they don't really know how to bring out the full potential of the Xbox.
column23: One game I got into recently on my Xbox is FIFA 12. I mean, on the whole it's pretty much par for the course for sports games, and EA Canada made it, so again, par for the course.
column24: In my opinion, FIFA 12 is so-so in quality. I like Xbox games usually, but EA Canada is not a particularly good developer, unfortunately.
column25: Little Nightmares is a pretty good game for the PlayStation. I enjoyed its focus on the single-player mode.
column26: Little Nightmares is a really good single-player game I was able to play on my PlayStation.
column27: I liked playing Little Nightmares on PlayStation. I usually enjoy games more on my own, so I didn't miss any multiplayer options.
column28: Metroid Prime Pinball is an odd little game to boot up on your Nintendo, but the multiplayer game does give an average experience all in all.
column29: Metroid Prime Pinball is an okay game in my view, but nothing too special. I normally enjoy multiplayer games quite a bit, but I'm not really a fan of playing games on Nintendo.
column30: I think Metroid Prime Pinball is okay, but multiplayer games on Nintendo have always bored me after a half hour or so.
column31: Visual Concepts is one of my favorite developers, so I enjoyed playing NBA 2K16. Though it being stuck on the PlayStation meant it couldn't quite live up to the potential of games that are truly excellent.
column32: I think that NBA 2K16 was pretty good. Visual Concepts knows what they're doing, and it's on the PlayStation which has my favorite controller.
column33: NBA 2K16 was pretty good. I honestly went in with pretty low expectations when I popped it into my PlayStation, but it seems Visual Concepts did something special with this one.
column34: Portal 2 is yet another amazing entry into Valve Corporation's gaming library. A downright perfect first person puzzle game with a great story and humor to boot! You must play it because really, there's just nothing like it.
column35: Portal 2 is an awesome game. I loved the first person perspective, and Valve Corporation is an amazing developer whose games are always my favorites.
column36: I think Portal 2 is an amazing game. Valve Corporation is an excellent developer, and the first person perspective of the game really enhances the experience.
column37: RollerCoaster Tycoon was really well made by MicroProse. It's a seminal simulation/strategy game and I enjoyed it a fair amount.
column38: RollerCoaster Tycoon is a pretty good game. I like strategy simulators like it, and MicroProse clearly knew what they were doing when making it.
column39: I've been enjoying playing RollerCoaster Tycoon lately. MicroProse knows how to make a quality strategy sim, and it shows in this game.
column40: I didn't like SpellForce 3 at all. The real-time strategy and role-playing genres it combines normally aren't my favorite anyways, but them throwing in a multiplayer mode just diluted the focus and made the whole thing a mess.
column41: I don't usually like multiplayer games, but I gave SpellForce 3 a chance just in case. Unfortunately, it was a disaster of a game that combined two genres I hate, real-time strategy and role-playing.
column42: I had thought the multiplayer would enhance SpellForce 3, but the RTS RPG was still lackluster.
column43: I think SpellForce 3 is really, really bad. It's made by Grimlore Games and their games are always terrible, but it also came out in 2017, which was an especially bad year for them.
column44: I wanted to like Grimlore Games' 2017 entry, but in SpellForce 3 they just didn't get anything right.
column45: SpellForce 3 is a pretty bad game. The developer Grimlore Games is clearly a bunch of no-talent hacks, and 2017 was a terrible year for games anyway.
column46: Blizzard Entertainment's StarCraft is a very good RTS, for real.
column47: StarCraft is a quality game. I tend to enjoy RTS games, and Blizzard Entertainment clearly knows how to make them.
column48: I think StarCraft is a fun game. Blizzard Entertainment's games are always decent, and I enjoy the real-time strategy genre.
column49: Stronghold 2 is okay, but I have some issues with it. It came out in 2005 and I tend to enjoy games from that year, but the fact that it's on Steam annoys me.
column50: For a Steam game released in 2005, Stronghold 2 is about average.
column51: Stronghold 2 is an all-in-all average game from 2005 among all those on Steam.
column52: Super Mario World is the one and only game for me! I think 1990 was the golden age for Nintendo EAD, and this game is simply la crème de la crème.
column53: 1990 was the year I first started gaming and I'll always have a soft spot for games from that year. And by far my favorite developer from that time was Nintendo EAD, which is why Super Mario World is possibly my favorite game ever.
column54: Super Mario World is Nintendo EAD's effort to create pure fun in physical form, experimentation which took decades and finally culminated in a great success in 1990.
column55: The Elder Scrolls Online is an okay first person MMORPG, I just wish it lived up to the series' legacy better.
column56: I think The Elder Scrolls Online is just about average. The MMORPG gameplay is fun, but it's held back by the first person perspective.
column57: The Elder Scrolls Online doesn't really stand out from it's peers in either a good or a bad way. I normally like MMORPGs, but the first person perspective was the wrong choice for the game, I would say.
column58: Tom Clancy's The Division was a pretty underwhelming Xbox game, mediocre overall, but that doesn't feel much like Massive Entertainment's fault.
column59: Tom Clancy's The Division felt a bit lackluster, but I think that Massive Entertainment games are still somewhat enjoyable on Xbox.
column60: I'm so-so about Tom Clancy's The Division. Massive Entertainment has not been doing a great job with their Xbox games in my experience.
column61: I like how Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness is now available on Steam, but it does not compare well to other action-adventure shooters on there.
column62: I don't really like games that blend the action-adventure and shooter genres together, and I also think that Steam is obnoxious, so I just really hated Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness.
column63: Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness is an overall poor action-adventure shooter, which shouldn't have even been released on Steam.
column64: If I'm going to play a trivia/board game, I'd rather just play an actual real life one instead of a virtual simulation. And certainly not one made by a terrible company like Electronic Arts, which is why their Trivial Pursuit is not for me at all.
column65: I really wish that the Electronic Arts' Trivial Pursuit game was good, but honestly, it was a complete disappointment. I await a superior trivia/board game video game.
column66: I think Trivial Pursuit is a waste of time. Electronic Arts has never had a knack for trivia/board games.
